content.value_statement: Rust Lambda functions can suffer slow first responses when binaries are large or initialization is heavy. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through concrete optimizations for build settings, dependencies, and deployment.
actual_capabilities: Suggests Rust release profile settings for smaller Lambda binaries.
Shows lazy initialization patterns using OnceLock.
Recommends dependency feature reduction and cargo bloat checks.
Explains ARM64 builds and deployment flags for Cargo Lambda.
Provides CloudWatch query guidance for measuring init duration.
limitations: Does not run benchmarks or inspect AWS accounts by itself.
Focuses on Rust Lambda functions, not every runtime.
Example deployment commands require user review before use.
Recommendations may need adjustment for strict latency or compliance targets.

use_cases.title: Tune a Rust Lambda Release Build
use_cases.description: Review Cargo settings and dependency choices before packaging a Rust function for production Lambda deployment.

use_cases.title: Reduce First Request Latency
use_cases.description: Identify eager initialization work and move expensive clients behind lazy creation patterns.

use_cases.title: Plan Cost-Aware Cold Start Mitigation
use_cases.description: Compare ARM64, provisioned concurrency, binary size, and dependency changes for an operational service.

prompt_templates.title: Check Build Settings
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of release profile choices.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Rust Lambda build settings for cold start risk. Suggest safe release profile changes and explain the expected impact.

prompt_templates.title: Find Eager Initialization
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of handler startup behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find eager initialization in this Rust Lambda handler. Recommend lazy alternatives using OnceLock or request-time initialization.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Deployment Options
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning across architecture, cost, and latency.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare ARM64, provisioned concurrency, and dependency reductions for this Rust Lambda service. Prioritize changes by latency impact and cost.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Measurement Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a cold start measurement plan for production. Include CloudWatch metrics, local checks, and rollout criteria.

output_examples.input: A Rust Lambda function has a large binary and slow first request time.
output_examples.output: Recommended actions: reduce release binary size, trim dependency features, defer expensive clients, and measure init duration before deployment.

output_examples.input: A team wants lower latency but must control monthly Lambda cost.
output_examples.output: Suggested plan: test ARM64 first, optimize initialization next, and reserve provisioned concurrency for strict latency paths.

output_examples.input: A handler initializes SDK clients before the Lambda runtime starts.
output_examples.output: Review result: move client creation behind lazy access, keep startup minimal, and verify the change with cold start metrics.

best_practices: Measure baseline cold starts before changing build or deployment settings.
Keep main initialization minimal and move expensive clients behind lazy creation.
Review binary size, dependencies, architecture, and concurrency as one optimization set.
anti_patterns: Treating provisioned concurrency as a replacement for binary and initialization work.
Adding broad dependency features without measuring the binary size impact.
Deploying command examples unchanged in production environments.

faq.question: What runtimes does this skill focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on Rust functions deployed to AWS Lambda.

faq.question: Can it measure my real cold start latency?
faq.answer: No. It provides measurement guidance, but the user must run benchmarks and review CloudWatch metrics.

faq.question: Does it change AWS resources automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides guidance and examples, and declares only Read and Grep tool access.

faq.question: When should provisioned concurrency be used?
faq.answer: Use it for strict latency paths after reviewing cost and simpler optimization options.

faq.question: Why does binary size matter?
faq.answer: Smaller binaries usually load faster and can reduce first request latency.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use this with existing projects?
faq.answer: Yes. They can apply the guidance while reviewing project files and deployment settings.
